sources.blog: https://shkspr.mobi/blog/2026/10/i-paid-people-to-try-and-follow-my-readme/ (Terence Eden, 2026-10-11, doi 10.59350/41s5v-7q247): bullet list 'Amongst the highlights I discovered were'
sources.commits: gitlab.com/edent/activity-bot fd68596..92089ff (2026-10-05 15:57 .. 2026-10-06 16:41 +0100; messages 'Usability feedback', '(user feedback)', 'following user feedback', 'based on testing', 'based on feedback')
sources.baseline_note: pre = fd68596 (last commit before the first 2026-10-05 session fix fa720be). fd68596 itself (2026-09-30, keypair order 'following user feedback') may reflect an earlier session; that item is excluded.

items.human: The link to the demo tool was wrong.
items.match: Says the key-generator file named in .env.example (tools/rsa_keys.html) does not exist / does not match the file list (tools/rsa_key_generator.html), or that the referenced tool path is wrong.

items.human: What does it actually mean to rename a file?
items.match: Says the instruction to rename .env.example to .env assumes the reader knows how/where to rename a file (locally vs on the server, with what tool) and needs explanation.

items.human: How do you rename a hidden file?
items.match: Notes that .env / .htaccess / .env.example are dotfiles that may be hidden or hard to create/rename/upload in file managers, FTP clients, Windows or macOS.

items.human: Should a demo tool be available on the web or just the user's local machine?
items.match: Says it is unclear whether the key generator (or the tools/ folder) should be opened locally, uploaded to the server, or is hosted somewhere; or warns about uploading tools/ to the public site.

items.human: Why does some text explicitly need to be quoted and some not?
items.match: Flags inconsistent or unexplained quoting of values in .env / .env.example (some quoted, some not), or unclear quoting/escaping rules for values.

items.human: My jokes aren't funny and are actively confusing.
items.match: Flags jokes/humour/snark in the docs (e.g. the GLaDOS/none-of-these list, 'Because I hate you', 'We live in the future now', 'Dunno', '*sigh*') as confusing, off-putting or unclear.

items.human: Some of the technical terminology needed explaining.
items.match: Names specific unexplained jargon a newcomer would not know (e.g. ActivityPub, Fediverse, WebFinger, keypair/RSA, .htaccess, subdomain, HTTPS certificate, DID, PHP-FPM).

items.human: The ordering of the different sections was confusing.
items.match: Complains about section order/structure (e.g. setup buried after a long feature list, no quick start near the top, requirements/setup/how-it-works ordering, steps out of order).

items.human: I hadn't actually explained what the software would do.
items.match: Says the intro does not explain what the user actually gets or what it is for (e.g. a Fediverse account at your own subdomain that people on Mastodon can follow), as opposed to a feature list.

items.human: A whole section which was technically interesting to me was utterly confusing to everyone else.
items.match: Identifies the 'How this works' section (htaccess rewriting to index.php?path=, data directories list) as confusing, too technical or not useful for users setting it up.

items.human: Not all web servers use permissions in the same way.
items.match: Notes that setup does not mention file/directory permissions or ownership, or that PHP/the web server must be able to create/write data directories (data/, posts/), or that hosts differ in this.
items.detectability: execution-likely (no permission text in pre; inferable only from hosting knowledge)

items.human: commit b5ea0e2 'Check cURL version (user feedback)'; README requirements add PHP cURL
items.match: Says the requirements omit the PHP cURL extension (README_nginx installs php-curl but the main requirements list only OpenSSL) or the extension list is incomplete with cURL named.

items.human: .env.example USERNAME: 'Do not include the domain name.'
items.match: Says it is unclear whether USERNAME should include the domain / full handle (user@domain).

items.human: .env.example REALNAME: 'real name' -> 'display name'
items.match: Says REALNAME / "real" name is unclear or misleading (should it be a person's real name? it is the display name).

items.human: .env.example password: 'You can also run on the command line'
items.match: Says the password-hash step is unclear for non-developers: where/how to run password_hash(...) or php tools/generate_password.php (needs PHP/CLI locally; shared hosts lack a shell).

items.human: commit 0c5112c 'Clarify the relative path of data' (/data/logs/ -> data/logs/)
items.match: Says /data/logs/ (or /data, /posts) is ambiguous: filesystem root vs inside the site directory, or where to find the logs.

items.human: commit 2b3f23e 'Make other servers like nginx more obvious' + Caddy instructions
items.match: Says setup silently assumes Apache/.htaccess, or that nginx/Docker/other-server instructions are hidden (only in FAQs) or missing (e.g. Caddy).

items.human: commit f204a54 'Clarify HTML support in README'
items.match: Says 'Only formatting elements are allowed' is unclear: which HTML elements are allowed/stripped.

items.human: Set Up: avatar/banner step now says 'Edit .env to include the image locations'
items.match: Says the optional avatar/banner upload step does not explain how ActivityBot finds the images (configure AVATAR/BANNER in .env) or where to put them.

items.human: Set Up rewritten: .env is the primary path, upload index.php, .htaccess and .env; Quickstart added
items.match: Flags confusion between the two configuration methods (edit index.php vs .env) or about exactly which files to upload (e.g. conditional '.env if you use one', .htaccess).

items.human: .env.example PAGE_SIZE: 'per page' -> 'per page on the website'
items.match: Says PAGE_SIZE is unclear (per page of what / where).

report_only.human: Some people read a README in the terminal.
report_only.match: Mentions reading the README as raw text/terminal, or that markdown/emoji rendering is assumed.

excluded_code_only: c91b465/b874f96 mkdir 0744->0775 and directory checks (code side of H11)
